items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: one of the trumpet players I had met in Buffalo, New York, when I was there with the Scott band. His name was George Hutchinson.

ctx.x: I was the only negro on the street, and when I saw who it was, I was mad enough to bite a ten-penny nail in two, but there was nothing I could do because I was in a southern town and the only negro on the street.

From Denver we went to the R.K.O. Orpheum Theater in Omaha, Nebraska. During the week, there was a dance which we went to after the last show. The name of the orchestra playing was called the Blue Devils, and one of the trumpet players I had met in Buffalo, New York, when I was there with the Scott band. His name was George Hutchinson.

He informed me that some of the orchestra were staying at the same place we were which was a very big rooming-house called the White House, because it was painted white. There was a room with a piano and one could buy bootleg whisky there. So we went to the White House after the dance which finished at 2 a.m. and started a jam session. The tenor sax in the Blue Devils band was a light-skinned, red-headed fellow and he told me his name was Lester Young.
